title: Dynamic Horizon Shepherd and Surge Credit Protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight operational policy and companion tooling (the Dynamic Horizon Shepherd) that allows teams to borrow and repay limited 'surge credits' across adjacent cycles. Purpose: reduce hard scope cuts for short-lived spikes, improve utilization smoothing, and provide a transparent ledger for capacity IO between product teams and platform. This ticket captures the product spec, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and initial simulation results required to ship the governance + UI + API for surge credits.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document reviewed and signed off by PM, Eng Lead, and Finance
Shepherd UI mockups in Console for assigning/consuming surge credits (desktop) reviewed by Design
Backend API to mint/redeem surge credits (rate-limited, auditable) has an RFC and implementation plan
Simulation shows >=25% reduction in emergency scope cuts with <=5% increase in cross-cycle risk metric
On-call playbook updated to reflect emergency credit reclamation flow
Pilot with two product squads scheduled for Cycle 2026-W13
tasks: Draft governance rules (max credits per org, repayment window, priority tiers)
Design Shepherd Console flows and confirmation states
Define API contract for credit lifecycle (mint, allocate, consume, repay, revoke)
Instrument cycle capacity simulator to model surge credit behavior
Add ledger events to audit log and wire to Console activity feed
Coordinate pilot with two squads and schedule retrospective
updates: 2026-03-01: Created ticket — initial idea surfaced in cross-org capacity review (meeting notes: https://drive.google.com/redwood/capacity-review-2026-02-28).
2026-03-02: Quick discovery with Eng infra and Finance; Finance prefers credit expiry (90d) vs auto-repay. Flagged as design decision. Assigned to Miguel Ortega.

2026-03-04: Design kickoff — Asha + Sarah Connors (Design) agreed on minimal UI surface: credit card in team header + modal for 'Request Surge' flow. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/redwood/dh-shepherd

2026-03-05: Engineering feasibility sync — ENG lead (Priya Shah) noted work in runtime autoscaling must be decoupled; proposed API gateway for credit checks to avoid per-request latency impact. Logged dependency ENG-1842.

2026-03-06: Simulation prototype run — initial model (baseline vs surge-credit enabled) shows emergency scope cuts drop from 18% -> 11% for medium-sized squads. Uploaded sim results: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/dh-surge/sim-results-2026-03-06
2026-03-07: Policy draft posted for feedback in #pm-capacity Slack — early feedback: ops requests explicit reclaim path for revoked credits. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-08: Security/Compliance high-level review — no PII impact; audit trail required. Security requested event schema for ledger; added as dependency for implementation.

2026-03-09: Product review with Growth and Core Platform — agreed pilot scope: Product Squad A (search relevance) and Squad B (conversations). Target pilot start 2026-04-01. Created pilot onboarding checklist.
2026-03-10: Updated spec based on Design review; added recovery SLA for revoked credits (48h margin) and emergency reclamation runbook. Next: RFC for API and Console mocks due 2026-03-15.
